title: Credits catalog
subject: credits
summary: What an app configures for credits: the currency, the services that cost credits, the price lists and the welcome credits.

purpose.intro: The credits slice's configuration is data: one call to `defineCreditsCatalog` in `shared/configs/credits/index.ts`. It validates when imported, so a bad entry fails dev, CI and boot alike, with every problem listed. The amounts in the seed are placeholders until product sets them.

reference.statement: The whole file, without its header comment.

snippets.caption: typescript

reference.statement: Keys are lower-case identifiers; amounts are whole credits.

claims.text: `currency`: the platform currency, a lower-case ISO code. One credit is one cent of it, which matters only where credits meet money, as with vendor credits.

`services`: what costs credits. `key` is what a consuming slice charges with (`metering.charge(owner, { service: "meteor", … })`) and what allocation rules and grants list; `name` is shown on screens; `unit` is what one charge counts.
`priceLists`: credits per unit of each service, per list. A service missing from a list is refused for owners on that list (the `entitlement` reason); a price of 0 costs nothing.
`defaultPriceList`: the list of an owner with no other assigned, such as an owner without a plan. It must exist.

`welcome`: credits given once to every new person (`user`) and organization, and how many days they last (`null` never expires). 0 gives nothing; it is the one source of credits outside access control, so an app turns it on deliberately.

reference.statement: With the payment slice mounted, the two catalogs are read together.

claims.text: Every plan key in [[payment-catalog|the payment catalog]] needs a price list with the same key here; the API refuses to boot otherwise. While the plan is active, its owner pays by that list.
Adding a service: add it to `services`, price it in each list that should include it, and charge with its key from the consuming slice's credits port.
